intent.raw_query: Nepal trekking Annapurna, $2000 solo, October 2026, 14 days

experiences.name: Annapurna Base Camp Trek
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic multi-day trek to Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m, passing through rhododendron forests, terraced fields, and traditional Gurung villages. Witness breathtaking panoramic views of Annapurna I, Machapuchare, and Hiunchuli peaks. The trail offers diverse landscapes from subtropical to alpine zones, making it one of the world's most rewarding trekking experiences.

experiences.name: Poon Hill Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Trek to Poon Hill viewpoint at 3,210m for one of the most spectacular sunrises in the Himalayas. Watch the golden light illuminate the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri mountain ranges in a stunning alpenglow effect. The relatively short but rewarding hike through Ghorepani village is perfect for nature lovers seeking dramatic mountain vistas without a full expedition commitment.

experiences.name: Mardi Himal Trek
experiences.description: Explore the lesser-known Mardi Himal trail, a hidden gem offering solitude and raw natural beauty away from crowded routes. Trek through dense bamboo and rhododendron forests to high-altitude meadows with unobstructed views of Machapuchare (Fishtail Mountain). Encounter diverse Himalayan flora and fauna including rare orchids, Himalayan tahr, and colorful pheasants along this pristine trail.
experiences.location: Mardi Himal, Eastern Annapurna Conservation Area

experiences.name: Traditional Gurung Village Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the rich culture of the Gurung and Magar communities in the Annapurna foothills. Visit traditional stone-paved villages, observe ancient Buddhist monasteries and prayer wheels, and share a home-cooked dal bhat meal with a local family. Learn about traditional farming practices, local medicinal herbs, and centuries-old customs that have shaped life in the Himalayas.

experiences.name: Annapurna Conservation Area Nature Walk and Birding
experiences.description: Join a guided nature walk through the biodiverse Annapurna Conservation Area, home to over 1,200 plant species and 500 bird species. Spot rare Himalayan birds including the Danphe (Himalayan Monal pheasant), Nepal's national bird, along with eagles, vultures, and colorful sunbirds. Explore cascading waterfalls, glacial rivers, and ancient forests while learning about the region's unique ecosystem and conservation efforts.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Annapurna, Nepal
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery — flight arrives at 22:30, so no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest and recovery — flight arrives at 22:30, so no afternoon activities scheduled
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 22:30. Clear immigration, collect baggage, and arrange a pre-booked budget taxi or airport shuttle to your accommodation. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort, freshen up, and get a good night's rest to prepare for the trek ahead.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a snack on the plane
meals.lunch: In-flight meal or airport snack
meals.dinner: Light snack from a 24-hour shop near the hotel or hotel room service if available (~$3–5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Late arrival — prioritize rest. Keep USD or NPR cash handy for taxi (~$10–15 from airport). Exchange a small amount of currency at the airport kiosk. Confirm trek permits and gear checklist before sleeping.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and enjoy a hearty breakfast at the hotel. Head to Thamel, Kathmandu's trekking hub, to rent or purchase any missing trekking gear (poles, sleeping bag liner, rain poncho) from budget gear shops. Compare prices — rentals are very affordable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Kathmandu Tourism Board office or a local trekking agency to obtain your ACAP (Annapurna Conservation Area Permit) and TIMS (Trekkers' Information Management System) card. These are mandatory for the Annapurna Circuit. Cost: ~$30 USD total. Explore Thamel on foot, browse local shops, and pick up trail snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to Boudhanath Stupa (a short taxi ride, ~$3) for a peaceful evening walk around the iconic Buddhist monument. Return to Thamel for dinner and an early bedtime.

meals.breakfast: Dal Bhat at a local teahouse near the hotel (~$3–4 USD)
meals.lunch: Momos (dumplings) from a street stall or small restaurant in Thamel (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Set meal (Dal Bhat or noodle soup) at a budget restaurant in Thamel (~$4–6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Permits are only issued on weekdays — confirm office hours in advance. Keep all permit documents safe throughout the trek. Buy a local SIM card (NCell or Nepal Telecom) for ~$2–3 USD with data for offline maps.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning tourist bus or shared jeep from Kathmandu to Besisahar (the traditional Annapurna Circuit starting point), approximately 6–8 hours. Buses depart from Kantipath or Machhapokhari bus park. Budget bus costs ~$5–8 USD. Enjoy scenic hill and river valley views en route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Besisahar by early afternoon. Check in to a budget teahouse guesthouse (~$3–5 USD per night for a basic room). Rest, hydrate, and explore the small market town. Visit the local bazaar and stock up on snacks, water purification tablets, and any last-minute supplies.
day_by_day.evening: Sit on the teahouse porch and enjoy views of the surrounding hills. Chat with fellow trekkers to exchange route tips. Early dinner and rest.

meals.breakfast: Toast and eggs at the hotel before departure (~$3 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside dal bhat during bus stop (~$3–4 USD)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat at a Besisahar teahouse (~$4–5 USD, often includes unlimited refills)

day_by_day.notes: Dal Bhat at teahouses often includes unlimited rice refills — ideal for trekkers. Carry at least 2 liters of water for the bus journey. October is peak trekking season — book teahouses in advance or arrive early to secure rooms.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the Annapurna Circuit trek! Start trekking from Besisahar to Bahundanda (approx. 12 km, 5–6 hours). The trail follows the Marsyangdi River through rice terraces, small villages, and lush subtropical forests. Gradual ascent with stunning valley views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking through Ngadi and Lampata villages. Arrive in Bahundanda (1,310 m) by early afternoon. Check in to a teahouse guesthouse. Explore the hilltop village with panoramic views of the valley below.
day_by_day.evening: Rest legs, stretch, and enjoy the mountain sunset from the village. Journal your first trekking day experience. Early dinner and rest to prepare for tomorrow's longer stage.

meals.breakfast: Porridge or eggs with tea at Besisahar teahouse (~$2–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks or quick stop at a trail teahouse for noodle soup (~$3 USD)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat at Bahundanda teahouse (~$4–5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Pace yourself — this is Day 1 of trekking. Stay well hydrated. October weather is generally clear and cool — ideal for trekking. Wear layers as temperatures drop in the evening. Trekking poles help on uneven terrain.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Bahundanda to Chamje (approx. 10 km, 4–5 hours). The trail descends steeply before crossing suspension bridges over the Marsyangdi River. Pass through Ghermu and enjoy views of Himalayan foothills and waterfalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Chamje (1,430 m). Rest and explore the small riverside village. Optional: take a short side walk to the nearby waterfall viewpoint (~30 min round trip).
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the teahouse, meet fellow trekkers, and enjoy the sound of the river. Review tomorrow's route on your offline map (Maps.me or Gaia GPS). Early sleep.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes or porridge at Bahundanda teahouse (~$2–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Vegetable fried rice at a trail teahouse (~$3–4 USD)
meals.dinner: Garlic soup starter + Dal Bhat at Chamje teahouse (~$5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Garlic soup is a popular high-altitude remedy — start incorporating it into meals. Avoid alcohol at altitude. Carry a headlamp for early starts. Teahouse rooms are basic but clean — bring a sleeping bag liner for warmth.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chamje to Bagarchhap (approx. 11 km, 5–6 hours). The trail enters the dramatic Marsyangdi Gorge, crosses multiple suspension bridges, and passes through Tal — the first village in the Manang District with a wide glacial valley and waterfalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through Karte and Dharapani to reach Bagarchhap (2,160 m). Notice the architecture shifting to Tibetan-influenced stone houses with flat roofs. Check in to a teahouse and rest.
day_by_day.evening: Walk around Bagarchhap village to observe the cultural shift in architecture and lifestyle. Enjoy mountain views at dusk. Prepare gear for higher altitude trekking tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Muesli with hot milk at Chamje teahouse (~$2–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Tsampa porridge or noodle soup at Tal village (~$3–4 USD)
meals.dinner: Tibetan bread with vegetable curry at Bagarchhap teahouse (~$4–5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: You are now entering higher altitude zones. Watch for early signs of altitude sickness (headache, nausea, dizziness). The golden rule: 'Trek high, sleep low.' Stay hydrated — aim for 3–4 liters of water daily.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Bagarchhap to Chame (approx. 13 km, 5–6 hours). Pass through Danaque and Timang with views of Annapurna II and Lamjung Himal. The trail enters pine and oak forests as altitude increases noticeably.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Chame (2,710 m), the administrative headquarters of Manang District. Check in to a teahouse. Visit the small hot spring near the river for a relaxing soak (~$1–2 USD entry). Explore the town's shops and bakeries.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a warm meal and rest. This is a good acclimatization point — take the evening slowly and avoid overexertion. Check gear and dry any wet clothing.

meals.breakfast: Eggs and toast with tea at Bagarchhap teahouse (~$3 USD)
meals.lunch: Apple pie and tea at a trail teahouse (Chame area is known for apple orchards) (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Pasta or Dal Bhat at Chame teahouse (~$4–5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Hot spring soak is highly recommended for tired muscles. Chame has ATMs and phone charging facilities — stock up on cash as ATMs become scarce higher up. Charge all devices here.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chame to Pisang (approx. 14 km, 5–6 hours). This is one of the most scenic stages — the trail passes through a dramatic curved rock face, enters alpine terrain, and offers the first stunning views of Annapurna II (7,937 m) and Pisang Peak.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Upper or Lower Pisang (3,200 m). Opt for Upper Pisang for better views and a more traditional village experience. Explore the ancient monastery perched above the village. Acclimatization walk recommended — hike 30–45 minutes uphill from the village.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset paint Annapurna II and Pisang Peak golden. Return to teahouse for dinner. This is a milestone moment — you are now above 3,000 m. Rest is critical.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and apple juice at Chame teahouse (~$3 USD)
meals.lunch: Snacks and trail mix en route, or quick stop at Dhukur Pokhari (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat with extra vegetables at Upper Pisang teahouse (~$5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Altitude sickness risk increases above 3,000 m. Do NOT ascend if you have persistent headache or nausea. Rest an extra day in Pisang if needed. Drink extra water. The acclimatization walk to Upper Pisang monastery is highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Acclimatization day in Pisang / trek to Manang. Choose the high route via Ghyaru and Ngawal for breathtaking panoramic views of the Annapurna range, or the lower valley route through Humde. The high route (recommended) takes 6–7 hours with significant elevation gain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Manang (3,519 m) — the last major village before Thorong La Pass. Check in to a teahouse. Visit the Himalayan Rescue Association (HRA) office for a free altitude sickness briefing (highly recommended, usually held at 3 PM).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Manang village, visit the local gompa (monastery), and browse the small shops. Rest and hydrate. This is a critical acclimatization stop — plan to spend 2 nights here.

meals.breakfast: Eggs and porridge at Pisang teahouse (~$3 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks or trail teahouse stop (~$3 USD)
meals.dinner: Pizza or Dal Bhat at a Manang teahouse (several have wood-fired ovens) (~$5–6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Attend the HRA altitude briefing — it could save your life. Manang has bakeries, gear shops, and even a small cinema for trekkers. Stock up on snacks and energy bars for the Thorong La crossing. Plan 2 nights in Manang for proper acclimatization.

day_by_day.morning: Full acclimatization day in Manang. Take a morning hike to Ice Lake (Kicho Tal) at 4,600 m — a stunning turquoise lake with incredible Annapurna views (4–5 hours round trip). Start early, go slow, and turn back if feeling unwell.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Manang by early afternoon. Rest, eat, and hydrate. Visit the Manang Monastery for a peaceful cultural experience. Browse local shops for last-minute supplies.
day_by_day.evening: Prepare all gear for the Thorong La Pass crossing tomorrow (or day after). Pack warm layers, gloves, hat, and headlamp. Early dinner at 6 PM, in bed by 8 PM for a very early start tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Tsampa porridge and hard-boiled eggs for energy (~$3 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks at Ice Lake or teahouse lunch on return (~$3–4 USD)
meals.dinner: Hearty Dal Bhat with extra protein (egg or cheese) at Manang teahouse (~$5–6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Ice Lake hike is strenuous but the best acclimatization option in the area. Do NOT skip acclimatization day — Thorong La at 5,416 m is one of the highest trekking passes in the world. Set alarm for 3:00–4:00 AM for tomorrow's pass crossing.

day_by_day.morning: THE BIG DAY — Cross Thorong La Pass (5,416 m)! Wake at 3:30–4:00 AM, eat a light breakfast, and begin trekking to Thorong Phedi and High Camp in darkness. Summit the pass by late morning (8–10 AM ideal). Enjoy the iconic prayer flag-adorned summit with 360-degree Himalayan views. This is the highest point of the entire trek.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the long descent (1,600 m drop) to Muktinath (3,760 m). The descent takes 3–4 hours on steep, rocky terrain. Arrive in Muktinath by early afternoon. Check in to a teahouse, remove boots, and rest immediately.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the sacred Muktinath Temple — one of the most important Hindu and Buddhist pilgrimage sites in Nepal. Watch the 108 water spouts and eternal flame. Rest and celebrate crossing the pass!

meals.breakfast: Light snack (energy bar, biscuits, tea) at 4:00 AM before departure (~$1–2 USD)
meals.lunch: Hot soup and tea at Thorong La Pass tea stall or High Camp (~$4–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Celebratory Dal Bhat or pasta at Muktinath teahouse (~$5–6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: This is the most physically demanding day of the entire trip. Start before dawn to avoid afternoon winds and weather. Turn back immediately if severe AMS symptoms appear. The descent to Muktinath is hard on knees — use trekking poles. Carry all emergency gear.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover in Muktinath. Enjoy a slow morning breakfast. Take a gentle walk around the Muktinath Temple complex and surrounding village. Visit the Jwala Devi shrine (eternal flame) and explore the pilgrimage site at your own pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trek or take a shared jeep down to Jomsom (2,720 m) — approx. 2–3 hours on foot or 1 hour by jeep (~$5 USD). Jomsom is a larger town with an airstrip, restaurants, and more facilities. Check in to a budget guesthouse. Explore the windy high-desert town.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Kali Gandaki River — one of the world's deepest gorges. Visit the local market. Enjoy a relaxing dinner and celebrate completing the hardest section of the circuit.

meals.breakfast: Apple pancakes and coffee at Muktinath teahouse (~$3–4 USD)
meals.lunch: Yak burger or noodle soup in Kagbeni (if walking via lower route) (~$4 USD)
meals.dinner: Thakali set meal (a regional specialty) at a Jomsom restaurant (~$5–6 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Jomsom has ATMs, phone charging, and internet. Thakali cuisine is a regional specialty — highly recommended. Afternoon winds in the Kali Gandaki valley are extremely strong — complete any walking before 11 AM. Book a flight or bus from Jomsom to Pokhara for Day 13.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Jomsom to Pokhara (20-minute scenic mountain flight, ~$100–120 USD) or take a shared jeep/bus via Beni (8–10 hours, ~$15–20 USD) for the budget option. The flight offers incredible aerial views of Dhaulagiri and Annapurna. Arrive in Pokhara and check in to a budget guesthouse on Lakeside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Pokhara's beautiful Phewa Lake. Rent a rowboat (~$5–8 USD/hour) and paddle to Tal Barahi Temple on the island. Enjoy the peaceful lake with Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain) as a backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along Lakeside (Baidam) promenade, browse souvenir shops, and enjoy the lively atmosphere. Treat yourself to a well-deserved massage at a budget spa (~$10–15 USD for 1 hour).

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Jomsom before departure (~$3 USD)
meals.lunch: Lakeside café lunch — pizza, pasta, or Dal Bhat (~$4–6 USD)
meals.dinner: Lakeside restaurant dinner — try a set meal or local thali (~$5–7 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The Jomsom-Pokhara flight is weather-dependent — have a backup bus plan. Pokhara Lakeside is the main tourist hub with ATMs, pharmacies, and gear shops. Rest well — your body deserves recovery after 9 days of trekking.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn for a taxi ride to Sarangkot Hill (~$5 USD) to watch the legendary sunrise over the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges — a bucket-list Nepal experience. Return to Pokhara for a leisurely breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the International Mountain Museum in Pokhara (~$5 USD entry) — an excellent museum dedicated to Himalayan exploration and the history of Annapurna expeditions. Optional: visit Davis Falls and Gupteshwor Cave nearby (~$1–2 USD each).
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in the Annapurna region. Return to Lakeside for a sunset lakeside walk. Enjoy a farewell dinner at one of Pokhara's best budget restaurants. Reflect on 14 incredible days of Himalayan adventure.

meals.breakfast: Full Western or Nepali breakfast at a Lakeside café (~$4–5 USD)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the museum café or Lakeside (~$4–5 USD)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner — Nepali thali or your favorite dish from the trip at a Lakeside restaurant (~$6–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Sarangkot sunrise is best on clear October mornings — arrive by 5:30 AM. Pack and organize gear for departure. Keep trekking permits and photos as souvenirs. Budget summary: Total estimated trip cost (excluding flights) approximately $350–500 USD for 14 days including permits, accommodation, food, and local transport.

trip_options.title: Classic Annapurna, Nepal Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery — flight arrives at 22:30, so no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest and recovery — flight arrives at 22:30, so no afternoon activities scheduled
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 22:30. Clear immigration, collect baggage, and arrange pre-booked transfer to Pokhara or nearest base accommodation near Annapurna region. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle in for the night.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — late arrival
meals.lunch: Not applicable — in transit
meals.dinner: Light snack or room service at the resort upon check-in

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Confirm trekking permits (TIMS card and ACAP permit) needed for Annapurna Conservation Area. Exchange some currency at the airport. Stay hydrated after the flight.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Spend the morning acclimatizing and exploring the resort grounds and nearby lakeside area (Phewa Lake if based in Pokhara). Visit the local market for trekking supplies and last-minute gear rentals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short orientation hike around the resort's surrounding hills to test your fitness and gear. Visit the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) for panoramic views of the Annapurna range and Pokhara valley — a gentle 1–2 hour hike.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Lakeside (Baidam) area in Pokhara. Browse souvenir shops and explore the vibrant street scene.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — try local dal bhat or eggs with Nepali tea
meals.lunch: Momos (Nepali dumplings) and thukpa (noodle soup) at a mid-range Lakeside café (~$5–8 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a Lakeside restaurant — try Nepali set meal or grilled trout from Phewa Lake (~$8–12 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase your TIMS card and ACAP permit today if not already arranged. These are mandatory for trekking in the Annapurna region. Budget approx. $30–40 USD total for both permits.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning drive or jeep transfer from Pokhara to Nayapul (approx. 1.5–2 hours). Begin the Annapurna Circuit / Poon Hill trek. Hike from Nayapul to Tikhedhunga (approx. 3–4 hours, 1,540m elevation). Walk through terraced rice fields and rhododendron forests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking from Tikhedhunga toward Ulleri if energy permits, or rest and explore the village. The trail involves a steep stone staircase ascent — take it at a comfortable pace.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into a mid-range teahouse in Tikhedhunga or Ulleri. Enjoy sunset views over the valley.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at resort before departure — packed snacks for the trail
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or noodle soup at a trail-side teahouse in Tikhedhunga (~$4–6 USD)
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner — dal bhat, vegetable curry, or pasta (~$5–7 USD)

day_by_day.notes: October is peak trekking season — trails will be busy but weather should be clear and dry. Wear layers as temperatures drop in the evening. Carry 2–3 liters of water.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early and hike from Ulleri (or Tikhedhunga) to Ghorepani (approx. 4–5 hours, ascending to 2,874m). The trail passes through dense rhododendron and oak forests. Enjoy spectacular mountain views as you gain altitude.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ghorepani by early afternoon. Rest, rehydrate, and explore the village. Visit local teahouses and interact with fellow trekkers from around the world.
day_by_day.evening: Warm up by the fire in your teahouse. Watch the alpenglow on Dhaulagiri and Annapurna South at sunset from Ghorepani ridge.

meals.breakfast: Porridge, eggs, and Nepali tea at Ulleri teahouse (~$3–5 USD)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or trail snacks — energy bars, nuts, dried fruit
meals.dinner: Dal bhat with seasonal vegetables at Ghorepani teahouse (~$5–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Altitude gain today is significant. Drink plenty of water and walk at a steady pace. Avoid alcohol at altitude. Book your teahouse room in advance during peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn start (4:00–4:30 AM) to hike up to Poon Hill (3,210m) — a 45-minute ascent. Witness one of Nepal's most iconic sunrises with 360-degree views of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), and Hiunchuli.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to Ghorepani for breakfast, then continue hiking toward Tadapani (approx. 4–5 hours through rhododendron forest). Enjoy diverse birdlife and forest scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Tadapani (2,590m). Relax at the teahouse and enjoy views of Machhapuchhre and Annapurna South.

meals.breakfast: Hot tea/coffee at Poon Hill viewpoint, then full breakfast back at Ghorepani teahouse (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Light meal at a trail teahouse between Ghorepani and Tadapani (~$4–6 USD)
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner in Tadapani — try apple pie, a local trail favorite (~$5–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill sunrise is the highlight of this trek — don't miss it! Bring a warm jacket and headlamp for the pre-dawn hike. The trail to Tadapani has some challenging sections.

day_by_day.morning: Hike from Tadapani to Chhomrong (approx. 4–5 hours, descending to 2,170m). The trail offers stunning views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli. Pass through the charming Gurung village of Ghandruk — one of the largest and most traditional Gurung villages in Nepal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ghandruk village if stopping — visit the Gurung Museum and admire traditional stone-paved streets and slate-roofed houses. Continue to Chhomrong if time and energy allow.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Chhomrong, the last major village before the Annapurna Sanctuary. Enjoy the warm hospitality of local teahouses.

meals.breakfast: Eggs, toast, and coffee at Tadapani teahouse (~$3–5 USD)
meals.lunch: Dal bhat or fried rice at Ghandruk teahouse (~$5–7 USD)
meals.dinner: Teahouse dinner in Chhomrong — try local Gurung cuisine (~$6–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Ghandruk is worth a longer stop if time permits. The Gurung Museum offers fascinating insight into local culture. Chhomrong has better facilities than higher villages — stock up on snacks.

day_by_day.morning: Hike from Chhomrong toward the Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) route. Descend stone steps to Chhomrong Khola, then ascend to Sinuwa (2,360m), continuing through bamboo and rhododendron forest to Bamboo (2,310m). Approx. 4–5 hours of hiking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Bamboo to Dovan (2,600m) through dense forest. The trail follows the Modi Khola river and becomes increasingly dramatic as the valley narrows.
day_by_day.evening: Rest at Dovan teahouse. The surrounding forest and river sounds create a peaceful atmosphere. Prepare for higher altitude days ahead.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Chhomrong teahouse before departure (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Simple meal at Sinuwa or Bamboo teahouse (~$4–6 USD)
meals.dinner: Dal bhat or pasta at Dovan teahouse (~$5–7 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Altitude increases steadily from here. Watch for signs of altitude sickness: headache, nausea, dizziness. Descend immediately if symptoms are severe. Leeches may be present in the forest — tuck in socks and pants.

day_by_day.morning: Hike from Dovan to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) at 3,700m — approx. 5–6 hours through increasingly alpine terrain. Pass through Himalaya Hotel and Hinku Cave. The landscape transforms dramatically as you emerge above the treeline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at MBC and rest. Acclimatize and take in the extraordinary views of Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Peak), Hiunchuli, and Annapurna South towering above.
day_by_day.evening: Early dinner and rest at MBC teahouse. Prepare gear and layers for the predawn push to Annapurna Base Camp tomorrow. Temperatures will drop well below freezing overnight.

meals.breakfast: Hot porridge and tea at Dovan (~$3–5 USD)
meals.lunch: Snacks and energy bars on the trail — limited teahouse stops
meals.dinner: Hot soup, dal bhat, or pasta at MBC teahouse (~$6–9 USD)

day_by_day.notes: MBC sits at 3,700m — altitude sickness risk increases significantly. Rest well and do not push too hard. Drink 3–4 liters of water. Temperatures at night can drop to -10°C or lower in October. Sleeping bag rated to -15°C recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn hike from MBC to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) at 4,130m — approx. 1.5–2 hours. Arrive at sunrise for breathtaking 360-degree views of the Annapurna Sanctuary: Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna III, Annapurna South, Gangapurna, Machhapuchhre, and more. A truly once-in-a-lifetime moment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the morning at ABC soaking in the views and taking photos. Begin descent back to MBC, then continue down to Dovan or Bamboo (approx. 4–5 hours total descent).
day_by_day.evening: Rest at Bamboo or Dovan teahouse. Celebrate reaching ABC with fellow trekkers. Your legs will feel the descent — stretch and rehydrate.

meals.breakfast: Hot tea and snacks at ABC viewpoint, then full breakfast at MBC teahouse (~$5–7 USD)
meals.lunch: Trail snacks on the descent — energy bars, chocolate, nuts
meals.dinner: Hearty dal bhat dinner at Bamboo or Dovan teahouse (~$5–7 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Reaching ABC at 4,130m is the trekking highlight of this itinerary. Descending the same day reduces altitude sickness risk. October weather is typically clear — ideal for sunrise views. Take your time and celebrate the achievement!

day_by_day.morning: Continue descent from Bamboo/Dovan back through Sinuwa to Chhomrong (approx. 4–5 hours). The descent is steep in sections — take care on stone steps and use trekking poles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest in Chhomrong. Optional: take a short walk around the village and enjoy views of the Annapurna range from a different perspective.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a celebratory dinner in Chhomrong. Reflect on the incredible trek to ABC. Treat yourself to a hot shower (available at most Chhomrong teahouses for a small fee).

meals.breakfast: Eggs and toast at Bamboo/Dovan teahouse (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or fried rice at a trail teahouse (~$4–6 USD)
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on dinner in Chhomrong — try buffalo steak or Nepali thali (~$7–10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Knees and legs will feel the descent. Trekking poles are invaluable on the way down. Chhomrong has relatively good facilities — enjoy a rest day if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Hike from Chhomrong back to Ghandruk village (approx. 3–4 hours). Take time to properly explore Ghandruk — a beautifully preserved Gurung village with sweeping mountain views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Ghandruk Gurung Museum and learn about the history, culture, and traditions of the Gurung people. Explore the village's stone-paved lanes and interact with locals.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight in Ghandruk. Enjoy a peaceful evening in one of the most scenic villages in Nepal. Watch the sunset paint Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre golden.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Chhomrong teahouse (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Traditional Gurung meal in Ghandruk — try gundruk (fermented greens) soup (~$5–7 USD)
meals.dinner: Local restaurant in Ghandruk — try Nepali home-style cooking (~$6–9 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Ghandruk is one of the most culturally rich villages on the trek. The Gurung Museum entrance fee is minimal (~$1–2 USD). This is a great place to buy locally made handicrafts as souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Hike from Ghandruk down to Nayapul (approx. 3–4 hours descent through terraced farmland and riverside trails). Enjoy the contrast of lush lowland scenery after days of high alpine terrain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange jeep or bus transfer from Nayapul back to Pokhara (approx. 1.5–2 hours). Check back in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a long hot shower and rest.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the completion of your Annapurna trek with a special dinner at one of Pokhara's best restaurants. Enjoy Lakeside's vibrant atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Ghandruk teahouse before departure (~$4–6 USD)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Nayapul before transfer (~$4–6 USD)
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner at a Lakeside restaurant in Pokhara — try Nepali-fusion or continental cuisine (~$12–18 USD)

day_by_day.notes: The jeep transfer from Nayapul to Pokhara costs approx. $5–10 USD per person. Treat yourself to a massage in Pokhara after the trek — many affordable options are available on Lakeside (~$10–15 USD for 1 hour).

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day in Pokhara. Sleep in and enjoy a late breakfast at the resort. Optional: book a relaxing Ayurvedic massage or yoga session (widely available in Pokhara, ~$10–20 USD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a peaceful boat ride on Phewa Lake — rent a rowboat or take a guided boat to the Tal Barahi Temple on the island in the middle of the lake. Alternatively, visit the International Mountain Museum to learn about Himalayan history and mountaineering.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at the Lakeside promenade. Browse the vibrant market for final souvenir shopping — pashminas, Thangka paintings, handmade jewelry, and trekking gear at good prices.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely brunch at the resort or a Lakeside café — try pancakes with honey (~$5–8 USD)
meals.lunch: Pizza or pasta at a mid-range Lakeside restaurant (~$7–10 USD)
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant dinner with Phewa Lake views — try Nepali-Indian fusion thali (~$10–15 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Rowboat rental on Phewa Lake costs approx. $3–5 USD per hour. The International Mountain Museum entrance fee is approx. $5 USD. This is a perfect recovery and exploration day before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Annapurna region. Early sunrise walk or gentle stroll along Phewa Lake shoreline for one last view of the Annapurna range reflected in the lake — an iconic Pokhara image.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out from Aegean Bliss Resort. Arrange transfer to Pokhara Airport for domestic flight to Kathmandu (approx. 25-minute flight, or 6–7 hour bus/tourist bus). Depending on onward international flight timing, explore Thamel in Kathmandu for last-minute shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Nepal with incredible memories of the Annapurna region. If overnight in Kathmandu, enjoy a farewell dinner in Thamel.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — treat yourself to the full spread (~$6–10 USD)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Pokhara Airport café or in transit (~$5–8 USD)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner in Thamel, Kathmandu — try Nepali set menu with live cultural performance (~$12–18 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Pokhara domestic flights to Kathmandu cost approx. $80–120 USD one-way. Book in advance during peak season. Allow extra time for airport procedures. Carry trekking permits and entry receipts as souvenirs. Nepal requires USD for most visa and permit fees — keep some cash on hand.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Annapurna, Nepal Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Poon Hill Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Trek to Poon Hill viewpoint at 3,210m for one of the most spectacular sunrises in the Himalayas. Watch the golden light illuminate the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri mountain ranges in a stunning alpenglow effect. The relatively short but rewarding hike through Ghorepani village is perfect for nature lovers seeking dramatic mountain vistas without a full expedition commitment.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery — flight arrives at 22:30, no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest and recovery — flight arrives at 22:30, no afternoon activities scheduled
day_by_day.evening: Arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to your hotel in Pokhara or Kathmandu for overnight rest. Welcome drink and late-night light snack upon check-in at Aegean Bliss Resort.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or pre-departure meal
meals.lunch: Not applicable — in-flight meal
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome platter at the resort — artisan cheeses, Nepali charcuterie, seasonal fruits, and herbal teas prepared by the resort chef

day_by_day.notes: Private airport transfer with a dedicated concierge representative holding a name placard. Luggage handled by resort staff. Ensure trekking permits (ACAP and TIMS) are pre-arranged by the resort concierge before Day 3.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late breakfast and resort orientation. Explore the Aegean Bliss Resort grounds, spa facilities, and beachfront lakeside area along Phewa Lake. Meet your personal trek guide and concierge for a detailed 14-day briefing and gear check.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided boat ride on Phewa Lake aboard a luxury wooden vessel. Visit the iconic Tal Barahi Temple on the island in the middle of the lake. Scenic photography session with the Annapurna and Machhapuchhre (Fishtail) mountain reflections on the lake.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's lakeside terrace bar. Enjoy curated Nepali fusion cocktails featuring local raksi spirits and Himalayan botanicals while watching the alpenglow on the Annapurna range.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet resort breakfast buffet — eggs Benedict, fresh-pressed Himalayan berry juices, Nepali sel roti with honey, seasonal fruit platters, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Light lakeside lunch at the resort — grilled mountain trout, quinoa salad with local herbs, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Fine dining at the resort's signature restaurant — five-course Nepali tasting menu featuring dal bhat elevated with truffle oil, slow-braised yak tenderloin, sautéed fiddlehead ferns, and cardamom panna cotta for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Use this day for full acclimatization and rest after the long-haul flight. Hydration is critical — drink at least 3 liters of water. Avoid alcohol on this day if possible to aid acclimatization. Confirm trekking gear rental or personal gear fitting with the resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private yoga and breathwork session at sunrise on the resort's mountain-view deck led by a certified Himalayan wellness instructor. Breakfast followed by a private transfer to Nayapul (the trekking trailhead) via luxury 4x4 vehicle — approximately 1.5 hours from Pokhara.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the Annapurna Circuit trek: hike from Nayapul to Tikhedhunga (approximately 4–5 hours, 1,540m elevation). Walk through terraced rice fields, rhododendron forests, and traditional Gurung villages. Your private porter team carries all heavy luggage.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at a premium teahouse lodge in Tikhedhunga. Freshen up with hot showers. Enjoy a private candlelit dinner in your reserved dining area with mountain views.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — Nepali-style porridge with ghee and brown sugar, smoked salmon bagels, fresh fruit, and Himalayan butter coffee
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet trail lunch prepared by the resort chef — whole grain wraps with grilled chicken, roasted vegetables, energy bars, dark chocolate, and thermos of herbal tea
meals.dinner: Premium teahouse private dining — garlic soup, dal bhat with multiple curries, stir-fried seasonal vegetables, and apple pie with cream

day_by_day.notes: Trekking permits (ACAP and TIMS card) must be carried at all times. Wear moisture-wicking layers and waterproof trekking boots. October weather is typically clear and cool — ideal trekking conditions. Elevation at Tikhedhunga: 1,540m.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning hike from Tikhedhunga to Ghorepani (approximately 5–6 hours, ascending to 2,860m). The trail passes through dense rhododendron and oak forests. This is one of the most scenic sections of the Annapurna foothills route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ghorepani by early afternoon. Rest, acclimatize, and explore the charming hilltop village. Optional short walk to the ridge above Ghorepani for panoramic views of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna South, and Hiunchuli peaks.
day_by_day.evening: Early dinner and briefing for the pre-dawn Poon Hill hike the following morning. Star-gazing session with your guide using a high-powered telescope provided by the resort concierge team. Early bedtime by 20:00.

meals.breakfast: Hot porridge, boiled eggs, whole grain toast with local honey, and ginger lemon tea at the Tikhedhunga lodge
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet trail lunch — smoked cheese and vegetable wraps, mixed nuts, dried mango, and a thermos of masala chai
meals.dinner: Premium teahouse dinner in Ghorepani — pumpkin soup, pasta with mushroom sauce, steamed momos with house-made chili sauce, and warm brownie with local cream

day_by_day.notes: Elevation gain today is significant (over 1,300m). Take frequent breaks and maintain a slow, steady pace. Drink plenty of water and avoid overexertion. Set alarm for 04:00 for the Poon Hill sunrise hike tomorrow. Temperature at Ghorepani can drop to 5–8°C at night — pack thermal layers.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up at 04:00. Private guided Poon Hill Sunrise Hike — trek to the Poon Hill viewpoint at 3,210m (approximately 45–60 minutes from Ghorepani). Witness one of the most spectacular Himalayan sunrises, with golden light illuminating Dhaulagiri (8,167m), Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Machhapuchhre, and over a dozen other peaks. Private hot beverage station set up at the summit by your support team.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to Ghorepani for a hearty breakfast, then continue trekking to Tadapani (approximately 4–5 hours through rhododendron forests). Enjoy birdwatching — the region is home to Himalayan Monal pheasants, eagles, and rare migratory species in October.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Tadapani premium lodge. Hot shower, massage session if available, and a relaxed private dinner with panoramic Annapurna views from the lodge terrace.

meals.breakfast: Post-hike power breakfast at Ghorepani lodge — scrambled eggs with local herbs, Tibetan bread with peanut butter and jam, fresh fruit, and strong black coffee
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch — tuna wraps, granola bars, seasonal fruit, and herbal tea thermos
meals.dinner: Premium teahouse dinner in Tadapani — tomato basil soup, grilled chicken with roasted potatoes, sautéed spinach with garlic, and chocolate mousse

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill is the highlight of the Annapurna foothills trek — this is the signature Poon Hill Sunrise Hike experience listed in your available experiences. Bring a warm jacket, gloves, and a headlamp. The viewpoint can get crowded — your guide will position your group at a premium vantage point slightly off the main platform. Photography golden hour lasts approximately 30–45 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Morning hike from Tadapani to Chhomrong (approximately 4–5 hours, descending and ascending through terraced farmland and forest). Chhomrong is a large Gurung village and the gateway to the Annapurna Sanctuary. Enjoy sweeping views of Machhapuchhre (6,993m) throughout the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Chhomrong and check into the premium lodge. Explore the village, visit the local monastery, and interact with Gurung community members. Optional visit to a traditional Gurung home for a cultural tea ceremony hosted by a local family (pre-arranged by concierge).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli from the Chhomrong ridge. Private dinner at the lodge with a special Gurung cultural performance — traditional Rodhi music and dance arranged by your concierge.

meals.breakfast: Full English-style breakfast at Tadapani lodge — fried eggs, sausages, baked beans, grilled tomatoes, and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet trail lunch — whole grain sandwiches with smoked chicken, pickled vegetables, energy balls, and green tea thermos
meals.dinner: Special Gurung cultural dinner in Chhomrong — traditional Gurung thali with sel roti, gundruk (fermented greens), dhido (buckwheat porridge), local goat curry, and raksi (millet wine) for those who wish

day_by_day.notes: Chhomrong sits at 2,170m. The ascent from the valley floor involves over 2,000 stone steps — take your time and enjoy the views. This is a milestone point — beyond Chhomrong, the trail enters the Annapurna Sanctuary zone. Permits will be checked at the checkpoint here.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and acclimatization day in Chhomrong. Morning guided nature walk through the lower rhododendron and bamboo forests below the village. Birdwatching session with binoculars provided by your guide — look for Himalayan Monal, blood pheasants, and Lammergeier vultures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spa and wellness afternoon at the lodge — traditional Nepali Pinda Sweda massage using herbal poultices, followed by a foot reflexology session. Journaling, reading, and relaxation on the lodge terrace with unobstructed mountain views.
day_by_day.evening: Private cooking class with the lodge chef — learn to prepare authentic Nepali dal bhat, momos, and sel roti from scratch. Enjoy your culinary creations as dinner.

meals.breakfast: Chhomrong lodge breakfast — muesli with yak milk yogurt, fresh fruit salad, Tibetan butter tea, and vegetable omelette
meals.lunch: Light lodge lunch — lentil soup, seasonal vegetable stir-fry with rice, and fresh lime soda
meals.dinner: Self-cooked cultural dinner from the cooking class — homemade dal bhat, vegetable curry, handmade momos, and sel roti with honey

day_by_day.notes: Rest days are essential for proper acclimatization before ascending into the Annapurna Sanctuary. Use this day to ensure all gear is in excellent condition. Check weather forecasts with your guide for the sanctuary approach. Stay well hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong to Himalaya Hotel (approximately 5–6 hours, ascending through bamboo and rhododendron forests). Pass through Sinuwa and Bamboo camps. The trail enters the narrowing Modi Khola gorge — dramatic canyon scenery with towering walls on both sides.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Himalaya Hotel (2,920m). Rest and acclimatize. Short exploratory walk along the river gorge. Wildlife spotting opportunity — this area is home to Himalayan tahr, snow leopards (rare), and red pandas.
day_by_day.evening: Private candlelit dinner at the Himalaya Hotel lodge. Stars are exceptionally bright at this elevation with minimal light pollution — evening star-gazing with your guide.

meals.breakfast: Chhomrong lodge breakfast — porridge with brown sugar and ghee, boiled eggs, whole grain toast, and ginger tea
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch — energy-dense wraps with hummus and roasted vegetables, trail mix, dark chocolate, and thermos of hot soup
meals.dinner: Premium lodge dinner — garlic and potato soup, pasta with tomato sauce, grilled vegetables, and apple crumble with cream

day_by_day.notes: The bamboo forest section can be slippery — use trekking poles. This is a significant elevation gain day. Watch for signs of altitude sickness: headache, nausea, dizziness. Inform your guide immediately if any symptoms arise. Temperature drops sharply after sunset at this elevation.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Himalaya Hotel to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) at 4,130m via Deurali and Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC) at 3,700m (approximately 6–7 hours total). The trail emerges from the forest into the open glacial valley — a dramatic landscape of towering peaks, glaciers, and moraines. Machhapuchhre's sacred summit dominates the skyline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Annapurna Base Camp — a truly breathtaking high-altitude amphitheater surrounded by Annapurna I, Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Gangapurna, Glacier Dome, and Machhapuchhre. Private champagne toast at the base camp (non-alcoholic option available) arranged by your concierge team. Photography session with a professional photographer provided by the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at ABC — the peaks turn golden, then pink, then deep crimson as the sun sets. Private dinner in the lodge. Early bedtime to prepare for the sunrise experience.

meals.breakfast: MBC lodge breakfast — high-energy porridge, boiled eggs, Tibetan bread, and hot ginger lemon honey tea
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch consumed at MBC — energy bars, nuts, dried fruit, cheese crackers, and hot soup thermos
meals.dinner: ABC lodge private dinner — hearty lentil soup, dal bhat with multiple vegetable curries, pickled vegetables, and warm apple cake

day_by_day.notes: Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m is the highest point of this itinerary. Altitude sickness is a real risk — ascend slowly, eat well, and hydrate constantly. Diamox (acetazolamide) should be carried as prescribed by your physician. Temperature at ABC can drop to -5°C to -10°C at night in October — full thermal layers, down jacket, and sleeping bag liner are essential. This is the most memorable day of the trek.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for the ABC sunrise — one of the most awe-inspiring experiences in the Himalayas as the first light paints the Annapurna massif in shades of gold and orange. Private hot beverage service at the viewpoint. Extended photography session with the professional photographer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin descent from ABC back to Bamboo camp (approximately 5–6 hours descending). The descent is much faster but requires careful footing on the rocky trail. Enjoy the changing landscape as you descend through glacial moraines back into the rhododendron forest.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Bamboo camp lodge. Hot shower (solar-heated), a well-deserved massage session, and a celebratory private dinner marking the completion of the ABC summit.

meals.breakfast: ABC lodge breakfast after sunrise — scrambled eggs, Tibetan bread with peanut butter, hot porridge, and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch consumed on descent — sandwiches, energy bars, fruit, and herbal tea
meals.dinner: Celebratory private dinner at Bamboo lodge — cream of mushroom soup, grilled chicken with roasted potatoes, stir-fried vegetables, and chocolate lava cake

day_by_day.notes: Descending from high altitude rapidly is generally safe but can cause knee strain — use trekking poles and take breaks. Celebrate the ABC achievement but remain focused on the trail. The bamboo forest section requires careful footing on wet or mossy stones.

day_by_day.morning: Continue descent from Bamboo to Jhinu Danda (approximately 4–5 hours). Jhinu Danda is famous for its natural hot springs along the Modi Khola river — a perfect reward after days of high-altitude trekking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Soak in the Jhinu Danda natural hot springs — a blissful 2–3 hour session in the thermal pools beside the rushing river. Private section of the springs reserved by your concierge. Herbal tea and fresh fruit served poolside by your support team.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight at Jhinu Danda premium lodge. Sunset views of the lower Annapurna foothills. Relaxed private dinner and early rest.

meals.breakfast: Bamboo lodge breakfast — French toast with maple syrup, boiled eggs, fresh fruit, and masala chai
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch — hummus wraps, trail mix, dried mango, and green tea thermos
meals.dinner: Jhinu Danda lodge dinner — tomato soup, mixed vegetable pasta, garlic naan, and banana fritters with cream

day_by_day.notes: The hot springs are at their best in the cooler October temperatures. Bring a towel and change of clothes for the springs. The Jhinu Danda springs are a beloved highlight of the Annapurna circuit — your concierge will arrange a private or semi-private time slot to avoid crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Final trekking day — hike from Jhinu Danda to Nayapul (approximately 3–4 hours, mostly flat and descending through terraced farmland and riverside trails). Enjoy the lush lower valley scenery and reflect on the journey through the Annapurna region.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury 4x4 transfer from Nayapul back to Pokhara (approximately 1.5 hours). Return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and enjoy the lakeside resort facilities — swimming pool, spa, and gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory sunset cocktail hour on the resort's private lakeside terrace. Curated Himalayan-inspired cocktail menu. Phewa Lake reflection of the Annapurna range at golden hour.

meals.breakfast: Jhinu Danda lodge breakfast — granola with yogurt, fried eggs, toast with jam, and ginger tea
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch on the trail — smoked salmon wraps, cheese and crackers, fresh fruit, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Grand celebratory dinner at the resort's signature fine dining restaurant — seven-course tasting menu with wine pairing: amuse-bouche, Himalayan herb soup, seared mountain trout, yak tenderloin medallion, Nepali cheese board, mango sorbet, and dark chocolate fondant with cardamom ice cream

day_by_day.notes: This is a triumphant return to the resort after 10 days of trekking. Inform the resort concierge in advance to prepare a special welcome-back arrangement — flowers, a personalized note, and a complimentary bottle of sparkling wine in the room. Book the resort spa for a full-body treatment this evening or tomorrow morning.

day_by_day.morning: Full luxury spa day at Aegean Bliss Resort. Begin with a 90-minute Himalayan hot stone massage using locally sourced river stones and aromatic oils. Follow with a traditional Ayurvedic Shirodhara treatment (warm oil poured over the forehead) for deep relaxation and nervous system restoration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided scenic flight over the Annapurna range in a luxury helicopter or small aircraft (pre-booked by concierge — subject to weather). Aerial views of Annapurna I, Dhaulagiri, Machhapuchhre, and the sanctuary you trekked through. Alternatively, private guided kayaking on Phewa Lake if the flight is unavailable.
day_by_day.evening: Private farewell cultural evening — traditional Newari dinner at a heritage restaurant in Pokhara's lakeside district, followed by a Thangka painting demonstration by a local master artist and a private performance of classical Nepali sarangi music.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast in bed — eggs any style, fresh-pressed juices, pastries, seasonal fruit, and Himalayan butter coffee
meals.lunch: Poolside resort lunch — grilled mountain trout with lemon butter sauce, Caesar salad, artisan bread, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Heritage Newari dinner in Pokhara — Newari samay baji platter (beaten rice, black soybeans, dried fish, egg, buffalo meat, and fermented vegetables), aila (Newari rice wine), and Newari sweets

day_by_day.notes: The scenic helicopter flight over Annapurna must be booked well in advance and is weather-dependent. October is generally excellent for flights. Confirm with the concierge 48 hours in advance. This is a premium add-on experience that offers a completely different perspective of the mountains you trekked through.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Aegean Bliss Resort. Sunrise yoga session on the lakeside deck. Leisurely farewell breakfast. Last walk along Phewa Lake shore. Purchase curated Nepali souvenirs arranged by the concierge — handmade Pashmina shawls, Thangka paintings, Himalayan tea collections, and locally produced honey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Resort checkout and private luxury transfer to Pokhara Regional Airport for the short domestic flight to Kathmandu (approximately 25 minutes), or direct road transfer if preferred (approximately 6–7 hours). Upon arrival in Kathmandu, optional brief guided tour of Thamel and Durbar Square if time permits before the international departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure preparation. Private transfer to Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu. VIP airport lounge access arranged by concierge. Farewell Nepal — carry with you the memories of the Himalayas, the warmth of the Nepali people, and the profound achievement of reaching Annapurna Base Camp.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — full buffet spread with Nepali and international options, fresh juices, artisan coffee, and a personalized farewell cake from the resort chef
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Pokhara airport or Kathmandu — Nepali thali or sandwiches depending on timing and transit
meals.dinner: Kathmandu farewell dinner (if schedule permits) at Dwarika's Hotel restaurant — an iconic heritage dining experience featuring royal Nepali cuisine in a UNESCO-recognized Newari architectural setting

day_by_day.notes: Confirm international flight departure time and work backward to schedule the Pokhara-to-Kathmandu transfer. Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in and security. The resort concierge will handle all luggage, transfers, and airport formalities. Tipping your porter team, guide, and resort staff is customary and deeply appreciated — the concierge can advise on appropriate amounts.
